title: Manicotti with Cheese and Meat Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Manicotti are large tube-shaped pasta shells stuffed with creamy cheese and baked under a savory meat sauce. The durum‑wheat dough holds its shape during baking, while the cheese filling adds a smooth, rich texture. The meat sauce is typically made from ground beef, tomatoes, onion, and herbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Italian “manicotto,” meaning “sleeve.”
Traditionally the filling is ricotta, but modern versions use mozzarella, parmesan, or even vegetarian cheeses.
The dish is a staple at family gatherings and Italian restaurants as a baked casserole.
The tubular shape helps trap sauce inside the pasta.
In Italy manicotti are often served “baked manicotti,” topped with melted mozzarella.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Cheese and beef provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: The cheese contributes calcium and phosphorus, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat sauce supplies B12, B6, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes in the sauce are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that helps protect cells.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Durum‑wheat pasta provides slowly digestible carbs for steady energy release.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The dish is rich in fats and carbs, so portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Lactose presence
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Prepared sauce often contains added salt; those with hypertension should choose a low‑sodium version.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional pasta contains wheat gluten and is unsuitable for those with celiac disease; gluten‑free pasta can be used as a substitute.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve manicotti hot, sprinkled with grated parmesan and fresh herbs. They pair well with a light arugula salad or a side of roasted vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Reheat until the internal temperature reaches 75 °C.
